clauses.reason: Executive Order 11496 (34 FR 18799, filed 1969-11-21) prescribes, under section 204 of the Agricultural Act of 1956, a regulation that, effective immediately, forbids entry or withdrawal from warehouse for consumption in the United States of Honduran fresh, chilled or frozen cattle meat and goat and sheep meat (Tariff Schedules items 106.10 and 106.20) during the remainder of the calendar year 1969, and does not apply to meat released under section 448(b) of the Tariff Act of 1930 before the date of the order. The regulation ends by its own terms: the restriction is stated to run for the remainder of the calendar year 1969. The last day on which it operates is 1969-12-31, recorded as the end date (inclusive reading); the alternative reading is that it stopped operating when 1970 began, 1970-01-01. Actor: Executive Order 11496 itself. The cited source is the order's own held text, which contains the words the remainder of the calendar year 1969. No earlier end is shown in held evidence and no later instrument extending or reviving it is held.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11496 (34 FR 18799, Federal Register of November 25, 1969; the govinfo PDF text layer), headed Executive Order 11496, Regulation governing the entry or withdrawal from warehouse of certain meat with respect to which an agreement has been concluded, signed by Richard Nixon in November 1969 and filed November 21, 1969 (the day number in the signature line is missing from the text layer; the census register gives 1969-11-21); number and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: three recitals under section 204 of the Agricultural Act of 1956 (7 U.S.C. 1854), then one operative regulation, effective immediately, forbidding entry or withdrawal from warehouse for consumption of the specified Honduran meat (Tariff Schedules items 106.10 and 106.20) for the remainder of the calendar year 1969, and a closing sentence that the order does not apply to meat released under section 448(b) of the Tariff Act of 1930 before the date of the order. The dossier's single whole-order clause covers all of this and matches; the recitals are not commands. Lifecycle: the regulation ends by its own terms with the calendar year 1969. The restriction runs through the whole of December 31, 1969, so the end is recorded as 1969-12-31 (the last day on which the restriction operates; the first day without it is 1970-01-01). The order recites that the Honduran export agreement limited 1969 exports to 14.1 million pounds, so the regulation has no purpose after 1969 and states no later term. No held instrument revoked, extended or amended it earlier or later. Searches: the U.S. Code, eCFR and Office of the Federal Register disposition-note searches record no hit for this order; a held-corpus search by number returns only this order's own printings.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings or continuation wording; its only exception, for meat released under section 448(b) of the Tariff Act of 1930 before the date of the order, narrows the regulation and is not a savings clause for the period after it ended. Entries and withdrawals refused during 1969 were completed acts. No continuing right or duty arising from the order after 1969-12-31 is shown in held evidence.
